caption: A line of flame advances across a stubble field with the wind, smoke drifting ahead of it.

sa.check: A line of flame crosses a stubble field.
The line advances across the field.
Blackened ground is left behind the line.
Smoke drifts ahead of the flames.
The smoke leans the same way as the flames.

pc.expect: The line only advances into unburnt stubble and the blackened ground behind it stays black.
pc.fail: The fire line retreats back over ground it has burnt; or blackened ground turns back to pale stubble; or the fire starts ahead of the line in stubble no flame has reached; or the burnt strip narrows behind the line.

pc.expect: The line advances the same way the smoke drifts and the stubble leans, and keeps that direction while they hold theirs.
pc.fail: The line advances against the way the smoke drifts; or the smoke drifts one way while the flames lean the other; or the line's direction swings about while the smoke holds steady; or the line advances while the smoke stands straight up and the stubble is dead still.

pc.expect: The flames point upward from the stubble, leaning with the wind, and the smoke rises as it drifts.
pc.fail: The flames point downward into the soil; or the smoke sinks and lies on the field ahead of the line; or the flames hang above the stubble with a gap below them; or the smoke pours downward into the burnt ground.

pc.expect: The stubble ahead of the line catches as the flames reach it and burns down to black ground behind.
pc.fail: The stubble ahead catches before any flame reaches it; or the flames pass over stubble and leave it standing pale and unburnt; or the ground behind the line stays pale with the stubble gone; or the smoke rises from ground the line has not reached.

pc.expect: The field stays a field of stubble that burns to black ground; nothing turns into anything else.
pc.fail: The stubble turns into another material as it burns; or the ground opens up behind the line; or a second fire line appears from bare burnt ground; or the flames pass through a hedge and leave it whole.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The field's edges, the trees around and the sky stay the same.
pc.fail: The hedges change shape; or the trees change into different trees; or the sky changes colour permanently.
